title: Characterization of bounded-error polynomial time
statement: For every language $L$ of bit strings, membership in the class of languages decided by finite nondeterministic Turing machines that halt on every random choice string of polynomial length and output the correct membership indicator with probability at least $2/3$ is equivalent to the existence of a polynomial-time Boolean verifier with polynomially many uniformly random bits that accepts members and rejects nonmembers with probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
